title: Putting a Revised Offer on Record Against a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Agreement
content:
Where the appraisal of a batch on a Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreement comes back other than the condition declared, a revised offer is owed to the customer, and the desk puts that offer to the customer and records it against the agreement.

**What the record holds.** One entry is written into the agreement's trade-in history holding the amount the offer now stands at, the ground the offer moved on and the condition the appraisal found, so the customer has the retailer's new figure in writing and can answer it. The agreement's own state is left where it stands; what changes is that the revised offer is on record against it and can be read back on the trade-in history.

**Recording it.** The entry is made through `put_revised_offer_f86761c2`, which the desk unlocks and calls itself.

**What the entry takes.**

- `tradein_agreement_id` — Id class. The reference number of the Renew trade-in agreement the offer is revised on, read from the trade-in agreement record found for the customer profile.
- `customer_id` — Id class. The customer reference number of the profile the offer is put to, read from the customer profile record.
- `revised_amount` — Fixed-format class. The amount the revised offer stands at, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the cent when it is recorded, and never negative.
- `revision_reason` — Enum class. The ground the offer moved on, exactly one of: `condition_worse_than_declared`, the appraisal found the goods in a poorer condition than the customer declared; `model_mismatch`, the goods that arrived are a different model from the one quoted; `device_locked`, the goods arrived still locked to a carrier or an account; `missing_accessories`, the charger, stylus or other accessory that should have come with the goods was absent; `market_price_change`, the price the retailer can resell the goods at has moved since the quote was given; `no_power`, the goods will not power on; `water_damage_found`, the appraisal found liquid ingress in the goods.

**What comes back.** A confirmation line in plain text naming the trade-in history entry written, the agreement it belongs to, the amount the revised offer stands at in USD and the ground recorded for it. The line being returned is what shows the revised offer is on record, and it can then be read back among the agreement's trade-in history entries.
